title: Nonsensical Structure Does Not Build Confidence
text: Studying French about 15 hours so far over a month. There are NO lessons or guidance in pronunciation. When you speak, the app will accept pronunciation that would mortify a native speaker. The app NEVER tells you WHY you were wrong. (ex. You used the singular, this is plural.) Only the bare minimum explanation for any examples. There’s no feature to drill (let me practice numbers, possessives, pronouns, conjugations, etc. until it becomes second nature.) NOPE. Repeating lessons is a clumsy process and you will not get new examples. Same material. You could memorize this and not learn a thing about how or why the French language works as it does. I am learning French IN SPITE of Babbel, not because of it.

title: Not as helpful as I’d hoped.
text: I bought subscriptions to both Duolingo and Babbel, thinking Babbel would be better for learning natural conversation. Two weeks in, I'm disappointed. Surprisingly, Duolingo’s game-like approach makes the lessons stick much better, even if the sentences themselves are sometimes a bit ridiculous. Babbel, on the other hand, is excruciatingly boring and feels like a strict college course. It lacks the helpful resources needed when a lesson gets confusing. Honestly, free podcasts and YouTube videos are doing a much better job supplementing Duolingo for natural conversation than Babbel.

title: I hope they address this!
text:

No need to think. The issue is that the focus becomes process of elimination and not critical thinking. Be creative. Change the spelling, put similar words, etc.

title: It’s ok
text: I use Babbel and Duolingo and Duolingo is a lot more fun! Babbel has a bit more focus on grammar, but the lessons and explanations are tedious and overly complicated, as well as being very prescriptive in how the lessons are structured (say new word out loud, write new word with letters to choose from, write new word in sentence from memory, from sound, in conversation, repeat), which is simultaneously hard and boring. I also prefer the repeating characters and gamification of Duolingo. It’s useful as a supplementary app, but there’s no way I would have stuck with it if I started learning German on Babbel first.

title: Customer Service
text: I had worked with the app for about 5 months.  I tried to devote about 5 hours per week and I started noticing that I was answering questions by deduction rather than answering because I understood the question.  This became frustrating and I stopped using the app about 5 weeks ago.  Unfortunately, I forgot about the app until I received the automatic renewal notification on my most recent credit card statement.  I did not receive an email from Babbel notifying me that they would be billing me in the coming days, so I could cancel, like every other auto renewal subscription that I have does.  (Incidentally, I also checked my spam folder and there was no notification there either. However, there were multiple emails asking me to upgrade to the unlimited plan.) Anyway, I asked for a refund because it had only been 4 days since I was billed but Babbel refused because of their “terms”.  If you don’t wish to be viewed as a scam I suggest you at least send an email to your recurring subscription customers, so they customer can decide if they want to continue instead of you deciding for the customer after you capture their payment.

It asked my language level (beginner, intermediate, and advanced, with no explanation as to what each meant) and dumped me into something way lower than where I should be - without any test or assessment. How am I supposed to evaluate an app for effectiveness when they use predatory “free trial” tactics to lock any meaningful content behind a pay wall? I will happily give you money - if your app works for me. Do better by your free users. I would not recommend this app.

title: Waste of Money for Starting.
text: If you don’t already have an understanding going in, you’ll get lost in minutes and throw your hands up. Spanish for example: “Yo” is supposed to be widely pronounced just as it’s spelled. However for whatever reason, they’re choosing a dialect to pronounce it “Jo”. That tiny example snowballs. title: Unpredictable
text: It’s a good app overall but it’s frustratingly unpredictable with how long lessons are going to take. One day a lesson will last 3 minutes, the next day’s lesson will last 15 minutes. They also have a great offline / download in advance experience that keeps your streak in case you go on a backpacking trip away from cell service.
